endorsements.quote: The guiding principle remains unchanged: each team member operates independently of the technical development, maintaining a purely clinical perspective that is not influenced by modeling or engineering goals.
For this reason, TIMA emphasizes governance structures as a core component of clinically responsible synthetic data generation.

unlisted_practices: Involve clinicians directly in every phase of synthetic data generation, from defining clinical rules to final validation.
Have clinicians review generated synthetic data for implausible variable relationships and translate their findings into binding rules for the generator.
Validate synthetic datasets by combining quantitative statistical measures with expert clinical judgment, using predefined acceptability thresholds before proceeding.
Have independent clinical experts blindly review a mixed sample of real and synthetic cases for plausibility and check the internal coherence of individual records.
Accompany synthetic data use in rare-disease contexts with careful monitoring, transparency about data provenance, and cautious interpretation of downstream model performance.

screen.reason: The paper empirically presents and tests the TIMA method (a structured clinician-supervised deployment/development practice) across cardiology use cases to assess how clinician-defined constraints and oversight safeguard the clinical plausibility of synthetic healthcare data.

primary.practice: clinician-in-the-loop multidisciplinary validation and constraint definition for synthetic data generation
